subject.title: [Feature Request]: Multi-lane concurrency support for sub-agents via sessions_spawn

question: Should spawned subagents receive caller-selected named lanes, and if so, what aggregate cap and lane-configuration policy prevents those lanes from bypassing the gateway's total subagent resource budget?
rationale: The current implementation intentionally has one scalar subagent limit; choosing lane identity, defaulting, namespace ownership, per-lane limits, and aggregate enforcement defines a durable public tool and configuration contract.

options.title: Bounded named lanes
options.body: Add a validated optional lane that defaults to `subagent`, with configured lane caps plus an aggregate subagent cap that continues to protect gateway resources.

options.title: Per-agent-only limits
options.body: Keep one spawned-subagent lane and address isolation through target-agent concurrency controls rather than model-selected lanes.

options.title: Defer orchestration lanes
options.body: Keep the scalar pool until a broader queue and scheduling design establishes shared limits and observability together.

recommendation.title: Bounded named lanes
recommendation.body: Add a validated optional lane that defaults to `subagent`, with configured lane caps plus an aggregate subagent cap that continues to protect gateway resources.

likelyOwner.reason: Existing sessions_spawn and subagent-concurrency history make this person the strongest routing candidate for the tool and queue contract.
